text: The lab README frames the full-observation experiment as reproducing the Pathak et al. (2018) benchmark. Which statement best matches the quantitative expectations stated in the lab and book?
choices: With N=500 the VPT should reach hundreds of Lyapunov times because the model is deterministic
A persistence forecast (predict next = current) already reaches ~5 Lyapunov times, so the ESN adds little
The Kuramoto-Sivashinsky benchmark is easier than Lorenz, so a single reservoir attains far higher VPT there
An N=500 ESN reaches on the order of 5-6 (up to ~12) Lyapunov times of valid prediction on Lorenz, vastly exceeding the persistence baseline of ~0.1
explanation: The README targets ~5-6 Lyapunov times VPT with N=500 (the lab docstring notes 5-12 in practice), matching Pathak 2017/2018; the book gives the persistence baseline as ~0.1 Lyapunov times. Option 0 ignores chaotic divergence (VPT is finite); option 1 grossly overstates persistence; option 2 is wrong because KS is higher-dimensional and harder, requiring the parallel-reservoir architecture.
